To address this, we propose an automated system for enhancing GitHub repositories' README files by injecting missing metadata, thereby streamlining contribution and issue management processes. My research is currently in its initial phase, and this poster outlines the problem, presents a proposed solution, and seeks collaborators for this endeavor. The ultimate goal is to develop an open-source tool that automatically optimizes README files to facilitate smoother interactions with GitHub repositories. 

  To begin, I conducted an exploratory study to understand the problem. This study focused on four research questions: (1) What information does a typical README file contain? (2) What metadata does a typical GitHub project provide? (3) How do maintainers update README files? and (4) What impact does a well-maintained README file have on a project? 

  The study revealed several key findings. Firstly, README files primarily include project descriptions, installation guides, and example use cases but frequently lack essential metadata such as contribution guidelines and issue reporting instructions. In contrast, metadata are consistently provided in other GitHub repositories, such as issue trackers and wiki pages. Moreover, README files are rarely updated, with some remaining unchanged for extended periods, and even then, they often do not incorporate the aforementioned metadata. Lastly, a well-maintained README file appears to have a positive correlation with a project's popularity, as measured by the number of stars on GitHub. 

  Based on these findings, I propose an automated system for enhancing GitHub repositories' README files by injecting missing metadata, thereby streamlining contribution and issue management processes. The system will be developed using a combination of natural language processing and machine learning techniques to identify and fill gaps in the metadata section. A labeled dataset will be collected to train and evaluate the classifier's performance. The proposed system will be tested on a set of real-world GitHub repositories, and its effectiveness will be compared to current manual methods.

Existing research on text style transfer primarily focuses on changing one aspect of language, such as eliminating profanity or converting informal writing to formal writing. However, this task is complicated by the fact that different styles often have opposing connotations. For instance, reducing the profanity in a passage may also alter its overall tone. To address this issue, we introduce a new style transfer task that simultaneously changes the language and tone of passages. This task is more challenging than traditional style transfer methods because it requires transferring both surface-level characteristics and underlying tones. We also develop a new dataset with multiple style types and create a new evaluation metric that assesses both the fluency and tone of the transferred text. We further examine the limitations of existing style transfer techniques in this new task and propose a new approach that uses a unified generation model to tackle this complex style transfer task. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method significantly outperforms the comparison methods in terms of both overall fluency and tone accuracy. The code for our research is available on GitHub at https://github.com/zhengyuwu/StyleTransfer. In contrast, 3D medical segmentation offers a more comprehensive and efficient approach, as evident from the recent success of 3D convolutional neural networks (3D-CNNs) in medical image analysis. This model is based on the standard stellar structure equations but includes an additional term representing proton capture efficiency. By numerically solving the equations, we have simulated stellar models of various masses and chemical compositions, up to 3 solar masses, and have identified the critical temperature threshold at which proton capture becomes significant. Below this threshold, as in our previous work, protons are not considered. Once the threshold is surpassed, our results show that in low-mass stars with sub-solar metal levels, protons may enter the core and participate in capture reactions. This effect is most pronounced in small stars with masses less than 1.2 solar masses and becomes less significant as the star's mass increases. irected Learning (GDL), a framework for developing intelligent decision-making policies, in the context of Reinforcement Learning (RL). GDL offers a moral and ethical perspective on RL by translating ethical objectives into algorithms that produce responsible policies. We demonstrate its effectiveness in training a decision-making agent to effectively administer a life-saving medication, Anti-Dote, in a Risky environment, resulting in a higher overall survival rate than standard RL methods. Notably, the GDL-trained agent not only achieves better outcomes but also learns to balance the trade-off between saving more lives and minimizing individual losses. This achievement is characterized by maximizing the average of the minimum of two opposing reward rates, an unexpected consequence of the GDL formulation. To our knowledge, this study marks the first instance of applying GDL to a scenario with conflicting reward structures. The underlying principles of GDL are also explored in relation to existing concepts in Ethics and RL. This model is typically applied using fMRI or PET data, with the former often relying on parametric analyses and the latter on simple summations. We propose a new, streamlined approach that combines the benefits of these two methods, leveraging the high spatial resolution of fMRI and the oxygen extraction fraction information provided by PET. This results in a more robust and efficient technique for estimating cerebral blood flow and the rate of oxygen utilization in the brain. We evaluate our method using simulated and real data from resting-state fMRI and 18F-FDG PET scans. The proposed technique offers a straightforward and reliable way to assess brain hemodynamics and oxygen metabolism in vivo, particularly when used with modern neuroimaging techniques like 18F-FDG PET and fMRI. This method can be applied to various neuroimaging studies to investigate age-related changes, compare different experimental conditions, or study brain development across different ages. The quality of compressed speech can be evaluated using various metrics, including perceptual ones, which simulate human perception and are suitable for this purpose. In this study, we examine the correlation between the mean opinion score (MOS) and the root mean square error (RMSE) of several algorithms used for speech compression. We analyze this correlation in relation to the type of compression employed, which can be either linear or nonlinear. We also propose a method to determine the optimal threshold for the RMSE based on the SRCC. The study's findings can be employed to assess the performance of recently developed speech compression systems. Additionally, we utilize these metrics to compare the quality of speech compressed using fixed-point and floating-point data types. This work showcases the potential of multi-modal data analysis and highlights the benefits of combining machine learning methods to achieve superior results. Finally, the potential applications and future directions of this research are discussed. It is expected that the findings of this study will contribute to the development of intelligent gaming platforms that can provide users with a more enjoyable and immersive experience. has been extensively explored in machine learning to enhance model performance by handling multiple tasks simultaneously. This has led to the development of various ensemble techniques that combine multiple models to achieve better results. Our research builds upon this foundation by introducing a novel ensemble method where the task itself forms the basis of the ensemble. This approach, known as Task Ensemble, involves combining multiple instances of the same task to improve performance. Since the task itself constitutes the ensemble components, the underlying assumptions of traditional ensemble methods do not apply to Task Ensemble. Nevertheless, we have theoretically proven that Task Ensemble can be viewed as an instance of the Generalized Temporal Ensemble (GTE), a concept we introduced. By casting Task Ensemble as GTE, we have established a mathematical framework for its analysis. Furthermore, we have shown that optimizing Task Ensemble is a complex problem and have proposed a sub-optimal solution based on the Variational Information Barrier (VIB) algorithm. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world data have demonstrated the efficacy of our proposed solution. The contributions of this research are three-fold: Firstly, it is the first to apply ensemble methods to task itself, presenting a novel idea in the field. Secondly, it is the first to conceptualize task ensemble as a Generalized Temporal Ensemble (GTE), providing a deeper understanding of the phenomenon. Lastly, it is the first to apply VIB to optimize task ensemble, presenting a practical solution to the problem. Notably, comments frequently blame specific individuals, but also express support for groups, with law enforcement and politicians being the most commonly targeted. The data revealed a significant correlation between the length of comments and the complexity of the opinions expressed, with more complex opinions often being associated with moderation. growing popularity of IoT and wireless systems.  To address this, there's a pressing need for efficient data collection mechanisms.  Traditional design methods focus on minimizing energy consumption, but they don't consider the data collection process' time complexity.  This paper proposes a time-optimal structure for wireless sensor networks, which uses an optimal surface area allocation algorithm to maximize information transmission efficiency.  The algorithm determines the best surface area for each node based on their distances from a central point, minimizing overlapping areas and maximizing coverage.  This structure can be applied to various disk-shaped networks and has been proven to achieve ideal coverage with specific node arrangements.  The results show that our structure can collect data in half the time compared to other optimal designs.  Additionally, we present a sub-optimal algorithm for practical use, which performs remarkably close to the optimal solution.  These contributions have significant implications for wireless sensor networks and offer better data collection efficiency.  The optimal structure was validated through simulations and proved effective even in dynamic network scenarios.  The sub-optimal algorithm was tested and shown to be close to the optimal solution in performance. To better understand this, researchers used a combination of computational methods, including molecular dynamics simulations at different levels of theory, to investigate the stability of aluminium ions in specific organic compounds. By examining the dynamics of these ions over a 1 microsecond period, they found that at room temperature, aluminium ions maintain a tetrahedral structure within these organic environments for at least 950 picoseconds. Furthermore, the simulations revealed that the aluminium ions exhibit more stable behaviour than their Magnesium counterparts, primarily due to the stronger bonds between aluminium and oxygen atoms.   Our dataset features 1000 training and 1000 testing images with 7 categories of shapes, along with 5 poses for each category.

  We propose several potential solutions to these challenges, including the use of more diverse training datasets, the development of more effective training methods, and the creation of theory-practice connections between understanding and learning.

 OSRA demonstrated superior performance over existing methods, while also being

is a digital document containing a patient's medical history, comprising various sections such as diagnoses, treatments, and surgical procedures. A pharmacist reviewing an EHR to determine a medication's safety may need to consult multiple sections, but doing so manually is time-consuming. To streamline this process, we developed a system that allows users to interactively search EHRs, enabling them to explore relevant information related to their query. Our system, built using a graph database and a web interface, facilitates fast data retrieval and visualization, thus aiding pharmacists in their review. 

  For effective graph database operation, we developed a strategy for indexing EHR sections and creating a search function. We also designed an interface for users to interact with the system, including features for zooming, scrolling, and clicking on search results. To test our system's performance, we compared its search capabilities to those of a leading search engine, using a dataset of 1000 patients and 10 search queries. The results showed our system outperformed the competitor in terms of precision and recall, with an average processing time of 50 milliseconds. 

  To further enhance the system, we integrated a recommendation component that suggests relevant sections to users based on their queries. This was achieved by applying the PageRank algorithm to the graph database and configuring the system to run periodically. The outcome was a notable 25% improvement in recall and a minimal increase in processing time of 5 milliseconds. 

  Our system's efficacy was verified through a user study involving 10 participants who evaluated the system's usability and performance. The study's findings indicated a positive overall system impact, with participants generally agreeing with the results and processing information quickly. 

  In conclusion, we have successfully developed an interactive system for searching EHRs that has shown superior performance to other methods and received positive feedback from users. This system has the potential to revolutionize the way pharmacists review EHRs and make informed decisions. Moreover, the system's architecture and algorithms can be applied to other similar tasks and domains.

The performance of our model was evaluated using simulated data and applied to real-world data from patients with non-small-cell lung cancer to inform treatment sequence decisions. The results demonstrate the feasibility of our model and its potential to inform high-stakes treatment decisions with limited data. Furthermore, the approach's ability to accommodate diverse data types and models makes it a versatile tool for a range of decision-making applications. Ultimately, the framework's capacity to continually update estimates with new information positions it as an essential tool for maintaining and updating clinical knowledge over time. Furthermore, we apply our method to the analysis of insurance claims and weather data, using the number of losses and loss sizes as functions of location and temperature, and identifying distinct patterns at extreme quantiles that cannot be captured by conventional mean regression or ordinary quantile regression. For example, at the 99.9% quantile, our results show that the lasso-penalized method correctly identifies a positive relationship between temperature and the number of losses in the United States, a relationship that is inconsistent with the results obtained from the standard lasso and ordinary quantile regression methods. 1054 is the most well-studied supernova in history, its precise type remains a mystery.  A recent study of the Crab nebula's X-ray spectrum suggests that its precise type may be 1SNR II-P or 1SNR Ib.  A new study of the Crab's optical spectrum, obtained with the 10.4m Gran Telescopio Canarias, reveals the presence of He I 10830 Å emission, a characteristic feature of Type Ia supernovae.  This discovery supports the long-held theory that the Crab is a Type Ia supernova, and the most plausible explanation is that it originated from a single, low-mass white dwarf star in a binary system.  This finding also resolves a long-standing issue with the theory of narrow-luminosity relations in Type Ia supernovae, and highlights the importance of further spectroscopic studies of historical supernovae. A comparison of the Crab's spectrum with those of other astrophysical objects reveals that it exhibits unique characteristics, and the most plausible explanations for its spectral features are that it is a very hot, oxygen-rich, expanding gas cloud, or that it is a very hot, expanding, gas-poor nebula surrounding a Wolf-Rayet star.   used for knowledge representation and querying data marked up with RDF or PG queries.

  but not both equally. This paper proposes a unified storage layer that can efficiently

  marked up with either RDF or PG to be executed directly without conversion. This is 
  achieved through a single query execution layer that can process both RDF and PG queries.
  The underlying storage is then optimized for query execution, leveraging existing indices 
  for the best possible performance. This unified storage is designed to provide a common 
  interface for applications working with hybrid data marked up with RDF or PG, enabling 
  efficient storage and querying capabilities through a single interface.

  measuring query execution performance and finding that native query execution yields 
  significant performance gains over converted queries. These performance gains are 
  attributed to reduced conversion overhead, improved index utilization, and streamlined 
  query execution. These benefits are observed across various query types, data sizes, 
  and system configurations.
